To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

wheel running is a highly reinforcing event, that it can support stable lever-press responding, and that it can be maintained at a stable rate by schedules that control lever pressing at rates that range from 0.5 to 1.0 lever press per second.

lever pressing was maintained by access to wheel running in 3 experiments, that the lever-press rate increased with increasing local rates of running, and that the lever-pressed rate was maintained at a stable pace throughout the sessions.

(1) the schedule parameters can be expanded gradually and the session duration extended indefinitely without disruption of the break-and-run pattern and (2) the rats that developed higher local rates of wheel running maintained more stable and higher rates of lever pressing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
establishing schedules with wheel turning as reinforcement.
the development of schedules that can be used to study the reinforcing effects of wheel running in the rat.
the development of techniques for establishing schedules of wheel running as reinforcement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
wheel running as a reinforcer is a powerful and versatile stimulus for the maintenance of lever pressing.
wheel running can be used as a reinforcer to establish and maintain stable schedules of lever pressing.
lever pressing maintained by a fixed-ratio schedule, a variable-ratios schedule, or a fixed-interval schedules of wheel access is not necessarily an example of "superstitious" behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
wheel running is reinforcing and can maintain lever pressing in a schedule of reinforcement, and that lever pressing can maintain running in a schedule of wheel access.

the schedules of wheel running maintained by lever pressing were very stable, that the schedules of lever pressing maintained by wheel running were very stable, and that the schedules maintained by wheel running alone were very stable.

the schedule parameters and the duration of access can be expanded gradually to establish schedules with wheel running, and the schedule with wheel running as the reinforcement can be extended to successive 2- and 24-hr sessions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wheel running as a reinforcer is not limited to the break-and-run pattern and can support stable rates of lever pressing at very long intervals.
lever pressing can be maintained by wheel running as the only source of reinforcement.
wheel running can be established as a reinforcer and that it can be scheduled to control lever pressing in rats.
